rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts, retaliation)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not end a covered tenancy without an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay or waive 2 months' rent as relocation assistance (3 months if the tenant is 62+ or disabled), give 30/60 days' notice, and offer to re-rent if the unit is offered again within 5 years. Buyouts are regulated and retaliation is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior/disabled) for no-fault terminations
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause
rules.effective_date_note: Division as retitled/expanded by O-21647 N.S. effective 2023-06-24; amended by O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies longer than 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities, dormitories, shared-facility rentals with live-in landlord, owner-occupied single-family residence, owner-occupied duplex, housing with a certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years, and separately alienable property (e.g. condos) whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and tenants were given written notice.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief and damages including punitive; at least 3x actual economic damages for wrongful eviction; at least 3x relocation assistance owed; attorney's fees; non-compliant notices void; City enforcement.
rules.interaction: Rights are in addition to state and federal rights; consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 but provides greater relocation assistance.
rules.review_note: Merged official ordinance text (D073) with Legal Aid fact sheet (D077), which confirms 6/24/2023 effective date.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property owned by non-corporate landlord with notice
dormitories, care facilities, nonprofit transitional housing

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels, and vendors may not sell or license it to landlords. Tenants can sue for injunctions, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.effective_date_note: Official text (D076) is the draft with blank passage date, effective the thirtieth day after final passage; June 2025 effective date comes from a law-firm alert (D002/D037). Exact day unknown.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Software publishing reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data more than 90 days old or public information that does not recommend future rents; software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees.
rules.conflict_note: Official document is a proposed draft without adoption date; enactment and June 2025 effective date rely on secondary source D002/D037.

unverifiable_exemptions: software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits

rules.title: San Diego source-of-income discrimination prohibition (unverified)
rules.requirement: San Diego has a municipal division prohibiting discrimination based on a tenant's source of income; its text could not be read, so details are unconfirmed.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 8
rules.quoted_span: Section 8 means residential rental property in which the tenant receives tenant-based housing assistance under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937, also known as the Housing Choice Voucher Program.
rules.conflict_note: Unverified: inferred from link-only source D075 (division title 'Prohibition of discrimination based on a tenant's source of income'). Supporting span is from D073, which only defines Section 8.

no_rule_findings.finding: No local rent cap found in the documents; the city's tenant notice points renters to the state cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: California law limits the amount your rent can be increased.

parsed.notes: San Diego: merged the two just-cause candidates into the Division 7 record, and merged the three algorithmic candidates into the Division 11 record. The Division 11 record has an unconfirmed effective date because the official text is a draft. No documents covered security deposits or application fees. The source-of-income record is unverified and rests on a link-only source.
